purpose: Section 30 requires this artifact regardless of branch. Because NEITHER the original 65-case study NOR the replacement-rubric holdout achieved the required detailed reproducibility (12, 17), Section 20's own gate ('before V2 may be evaluated against it') is NOT satisfied. This artifact therefore does NOT certify a V2-vs-ground-truth score. What follows is explicitly informational/diagnostic disclosure only, computed at zero cost from data already produced (no live-judge calls were made for this artifact - see 22).
formalStatus: NOT_A_CERTIFIED_EVALUATION - no reproducible independent consensus exists on the detailed dimension in either sample, so V2's detailed-state performance cannot be meaningfully scored against a validated human ground truth. Per Section 37, this is precisely what NEEDS_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION means: Headroom does not yet have a trustworthy INSTRUMENT for this measurement.

informationalBinaryComparison.caveat: Binary credit/no-credit WAS independently reproducible in both samples (94.9% original, 97.0% holdout, both >=90%). This binary-only comparison is disclosed for its diagnostic value, but is explicitly NOT a certifying pass/fail evaluation, since Section 20's conjunctive requirement (binary AND detailed) for 'V2 may be evaluated against it' was never met.
informationalBinaryComparison.method: V2's own deterministic binaryDisposition (derived from the sealed matchStatus label: CREDIT iff matchStatus in {EXACT_SINGLE, EXACT_COMPOSITE}, else NO_CREDIT - the same convention used throughout this session) compared against the 2-of-3 majority binary consensus of the three independent adjudicators, computed entirely from already-produced sealed labels and adjudicator results (zero additional cost).

originalSample.disagreementDirection: All 9 disagreements are V2 under-crediting relative to the consensus (V2 says NO_CREDIT, humans say CREDIT) - zero cases of V2 over-crediting on this sample. Consistent with the deterministic-only engine being conservative, not with a false-credit risk.

holdoutSample.disagreementDirection: All 3 disagreements here are the OPPOSITE direction - V2 says CREDIT, consensus says NO_CREDIT. Given the detailed-taxonomy unreliability demonstrated by this same holdout (17), this is NOT presented as proof V2 over-credited - it is equally possible the 3 adjudicators (working from a rubric already shown to be imprecise) under-credited a genuinely correct representation. Flagged as an open item for manual review in 24-remaining-evaluator-risks.json, not as a confirmed false credit.

detailedComparisonNotAttempted: No V2-vs-consensus DETAILED state comparison is reported, since no detailed consensus achieved the required reproducibility on either sample - producing such a number would imply a precision the underlying instrument does not have, which Section 37 explicitly warns against.
falseCreditControlCrossCheck: See 20-known-false-credit-regression.json - this is the one comparison that IS certified, because the false-credit determination is binary, unanimous across all 3 independent adjudicators on all 14 controls, AND corroborated by V2's own frozen deterministic engine (03-matcher-remediation.json / dsgr-false-credit-gate.test.ts).
